name: Central bank stress
summary: Bank of England raised rates to 4% on 5 Nov; ECB held at 2.5% with a December rise in view and Lagarde leaving early
state: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since August 2023; eight of nine members backed it and one sought 4.25%. It forecasts inflation near 5% in Q2 2027 (Trustnet). The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.5% on 29 Oct after rises in June and September, analysts expect a possible rise on 17 Dec, and Lagarde said she will step down on 7 Feb 2027 (Brussels Signal). Policymakers face higher inflation and weaker growth; no emergency or inter-meeting move was found as of 8 Nov.
for_you: Borrowers whose loan rates reset soon are most exposed to rises in central-bank rates. Rates paid on savings tend to follow with a lag.
rubric_hit: Stagflationary dilemma (Watch line); no emergency inter-meeting move or attempt to remove a central-bank head found

sources.title: Trustnet — Bank of England raises interest rates to 4% with hints of more to come
Brussels Signal — ECB holds rates despite inflation alarm as Lagarde prepares early exit

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
